parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is one of documented, violent enforcement: the 2014 act (10-14 years) is used by police as an extortion and abuse lever against people perceived as gender-nonconforming ('looked gay'), with torture, mass hotel raids and arbitrary arrests recorded across multiple years. A trans woman was killed in the capital with no arrests six months on, and official response included misgendering; the state has no protections and no recourse functions. Religious-law death-penalty exposure exists in twelve northern provinces, and dating-app luring gangs target the outed with beating, filming and blackmail — a direct traveller exposure. Custody placement is discretionary and has placed a trans woman in a male, maximum-security facility. This sits at the lower edge of the 0.25 band: less than the execution-anchored 0.05 tier, because the capital penalty attaches to same-sex conduct rather than identity, but materially worse than jurisdictions with merely corrupt or administrative enforcement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Discretionary placement of trans women, including maximum-security male custody (2024 case); long pre-trial detention documented (2007-2011 group).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A panel found the maximum-security placement breached the corrections statute — procedural finding only, no documented operative remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest under the act or perception-based policing leads into custody with placement at official discretion.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Religious criminal law with death penalty for male same-sex acts in twelve northern provinces; enforcement varies by territory.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Territorial location determines which regime — secular 14-year or religious capital — applies.

care_services.exposure: LGBTQ+ people fear seeking medical care or reporting crimes due to arrest and extortion risk; law hampers HIV services.
care_services.protection: Constitutional health guarantee exists on paper alongside criminalisation; education-sector non-discrimination policy including sexual orientation.
care_services.interaction: Fear of disclosure reaches any clinical encounter.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police torture, arbitrary arrest, extortion for 'looking gay'; mass hotel raids (100+ arrests, 2018-2023); state framing treats gender-nonconforming people as criminal targets.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None documented; no political party endorses LGBTQ+ rights.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The national act weaponises policing across all territories.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for visiting minors specifically; general criminalisation climate applies.
minors_guardians.protection: Schools policy prohibits discrimination on sexual orientation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented killing of a trans woman with impunity; no arrests six months on; police misgendered the victim; luring gangs beat, film and blackmail via dating apps — a direct exposure for visitors using such apps.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None: no legal protections for LGBTQ+ people; community self-protection forums are the only documented response.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police non-response confirms the impunity environment.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Cross-dressing criminalisation proposals reported (2022) — not enacted, creating forward uncertainty; no published prosecution figures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: No functioning remedy channel exists at any level.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor involves terminal extortion and short cells under a vagrancy lever; this dossier's enforcement is more severe — documented torture under the act, a killing with impunity, and 10-14-year custodial maxima — so it rates materially below.

Similar structure: presentation-driven police abuse, custody violence, capital provisions not yet applied to identity, and illusory remedies. This case is slightly less extreme because no trans-specific execution pathway is documented and the documented custodial case was short, but it sits close to that tier.

That anchor features administrative friction, humiliation and rare prosecutions. Here enforcement is violent and predatory — mass raids, torture, a killed trans woman, app-luring blackmail — far beyond the 0.45 tier; rating much lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a nationally criminalising state whose enforcement machinery demonstrably targets people perceived as gender-nonconforming through torture, extortion, mass raids and app-lured blackmail, with a religious-capital layer in the north and documented impunity for the killing of a trans woman, compounded by official misgendering and discretionary male-custody placement. No protective institution operates at any level for an outed visitor; the only documented recourse (a corrections-statute finding) changed nothing for the detainee. Severity is high (imprisonment, custodial violence, killing with impunity, capital religious provisions) and frequency is real for anyone outed or using dating apps, placing the jurisdiction at the upper boundary of the Severe Risk band: a traveller who is outed faces probable predatory state and criminal exploitation rather than a functioning, tolerant society.
